messages:
maria: Quick note — I ran a compact region-by-region cost + latency probe for our inference fleets. Looking for quick alignment on where to size commitments vs keep on-demand/spot. TL;DR: us-central H100 commitments give best $/inference for low-latency traffic; asia-southeast still expensive on egress and maintenance.
ajay: Can you paste the numbers? even ballpark is fine. Also include expected utilization assumptions.
maria: sure — assumptions first: 70% util for reserved GPU pools (steady-state), 30% util for spot-backed burst. 1y commitments vs on-demand. Model mix: 60% streaming LLM (latency-sensitive), 40% embedding/batch. Costs below are all raw infra cost per GPU-hour (excl. SW/ops):
```
Region          | GPU   | 1y-res $/hr | on-demand $/hr | egress $/GB
us-central1     | H100  | 3.40        | 5.10           | 0.09
us-west1        | A100  | 2.10        | 3.10           | 0.085
eu-west1        | A100  | 2.35        | 3.40           | 0.12
asia-southeast1 | A100  | 2.75        | 4.50           | 0.20
```
Notes: cloud vendor gives ~33% discount for 1y reserved for H100 in us-central given our committed volumes; 1y on A100 ~32% typical. Egress varies a lot for EU/Asia. These are normalized across instance classes.
lucy: Nice. How sensitive is model latency to region? percent tail latency increase if we place eu users in us-central?
maria: Measured p95 increase ~80–110ms for eu-west -> us-central for chat flows (due to RTT + proxying). For embeddings (async) it's fine. So latency-sensitive endpoints for EU must be regional or routed through edge caching.
ted: What about reserved commitments for smaller regions? Are we committing in eu-west1 or just us-central + us-west? We want to avoid stranded capacity/underutilization.
maria: Proposal: commit primary pool in us-central (H100) to cover global baseline 55% of peak streaming capacity; commit smaller A100 pool in us-west1 for west coast redundancy and burst; keep eu-west1 and asia as on-demand/reserved-shelf hybrid: short-term 6mo reserved for predictable base (embedding-heavy customers) and on-demand for spike. This minimizes stranded capacity while keeping low-latency hotspots regional.
infra-bot: billing-alert: projected monthly variance vs prior commit plan: +18% for asia network egress and +6% for cross-region replication. See billing dashboard: https://redwood.internal/billing/proj/17653
ajay: For the math — assuming 70% util on reserved H100 pool in us-central with 1y-res at $3.40/hr, what's effective $/inference for our avg streaming token mix? we need to show this to finance.
maria: Quick calc (ballpark): avg tokens/session 120, token cost in compute ~0.012 GPU-hr per 1000 tokens (streaming optimized). So at 70% util: effective hourly cost per GPU ~3.40/0.7 = 4.86 $/hr. Per 1k tokens -> 4.86 * 0.012 = $0.058 per 1k tokens. On-demand at 5.10/hr -> 5.10/0.7*0.012 = $0.087 per 1k tokens. So ~33% saving per token with committed H100 in us-central.
lucy: That seems compelling. But we need to factor in egress for EU users if we centralize: 0.12 $/GB -> how many GB per 1k tokens? roughly 0.002 GB? (very small) — so egress is non-trivial only for heavy embedding or dataset transfers.
cost-ops: A few practical notes: 1) vendor contract: 1y-res has a quarterly true-up window — we can increase but not decrease committed units without penalty. 2) 3y gives more discount but kills flexibility for model shifts. 3) consider convertible reservations where available.
ajay: Can we do a mixed commit: commit 60% of baseline streaming in us-central H100, 20% in us-west1 A100, leave 20% for on-demand across regions? That would reduce risk of being locked in.
maria: Yes — that maps to utilization profile we saw. Additionally, put geo-rules: route EU latency-critical traffic to eu-west1 on on-demand/A100 and fall back to us-central reserved only when local capacity depleted (with optional degraded SLO). That keeps most EU traffic local, saving p95 and lowering egress.
ted: Any network constraints for cross-region cache sync? how often do KV caches replicate?
maria: Currently we replicate prefix caches every 15m for warm-start across regions; that adds modest cross-region bandwidth (~0.2 TB/day for our active models). If we reduce replication frequency to 1h for non-critical models, we can save ~60% of that egress.
cost-ops: Action items: 1) maria to publish a short commit sizing spreadsheet with per-region commit recommendations + risk bands (due EOD Thursday). 2) ajay to run a 2-week canary routing test: keep streaming baseline in us-central commit pattern but route 25% eu traffic to us-central to observe tail effects. 3) infra to check quota limits for H100 in us-central if we push commit to vendor.
maria: I'll drop the spreadsheet in #eng-infra later today. For now: recommended commit footprint (1y): us-central H100 = 110 GPUs reserved, us-west1 A100 = 40 GPUs reserved, eu-west1 = 0 initial 1y reserved (6mo shelf only), asia-southeast1 = 0 reserved (on-demand). These numbers assume our Q3 traffic forecast.
ajay: Looks good. One more ask — include the amortized ops+SRE overhead per GPU (~$0.30/hr) in the spreadsheet so finance can see TCO.
maria: will do. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: note: scheduled quota increase request for us-central H100 GPUs submitted (req id 78921).
